facts.text: Curiosity Rover was deployed at Gale Crater during Curiosity (MSL) in 2012.

Curiosity is a car-sized rover that landed on 6 August 2012 using an audacious sky crane manoeuvre. Weighing 899 kg, it is powered by a plutonium-238 radioisotope thermoelectric generator, so unlike Spirit and Opportunity, dust storms cannot end its mission. Curiosity carries 10 science instruments and has been climbing Mount Sharp since 2014.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Confirmed that Gale Crater once held a habitable freshwater lake environment with all six elements essential for life.
Still operational and climbing Mount Sharp as of 2024, having driven over 30 km and drilled dozens of rock samples.
